main_text.p: aduersarius, tanq́ si exceptum es- set, ita dicit se secutū. Vtetur exem- plis iis, quibus idem scriptor: aut si id non poterit, quibus alij, quod ex cipiendum putarint, exceperint. Quæreda etiam ratio est, si qua po- terit inueniri, quare nō sit exceptū: aut iniqua lex, aut inutilis futura di- cetur, aut alia caussa obtemperādi, alia abrogandi: dissentire aduersa- rij uocem, atq̈ legis. Deinde amplí ficandi caussa, de conseruandis legi bus, de periculo rerumpublicarum atq̈ priuatarū, cùm aliis locis, tum in perorādo maxime, grauiter erit, uehementerq̈ dicendum.

p.i: Cum autem aliud scriptor sensisse uidetur.) Scripti et sententiæ cōtroucrsia pluribus expli catur, propterea quod difficiliorem habeat do- ctrinam, usumq; maiorem. incidit enim sæpissi- mè in legibus explicandis, in testamentis, in in- terdictis, in religionis controuersijs, ac deniq; in omnium autorum explicatione. Primum igitur Cicero cum instituit, qui scriptū defendat: post etiam, qui sententiā. Hæc autè scriptū tuentis in- stitu-

page.notes: Marginal mark at left beside "uehementerq dicendum" is a dash only. Small marks at right margin of the last paragraph are scan artifacts, not transcribed. Possible misreadings: "si qua po- terit" reads "poterit" (line break); "sententiā" and "defendat" uncertain. Printed "stitu-" ends the page with a hyphen; the catchword "ritu." is not separately printed and is given only as the word completing the hyphenated line, so it should be removed if not confirmed.
